historical_record.description: The Stanyan House: a prefabricated wooden building shipped by sea from Boston and erected here between 1852 and 1854, from the earliest period of building in the Western Addition and among the oldest houses in San Francisco.
Apartments were added on each side of the house in 1885 for the extended family of Supervisor Charles Stanyan, for whom Stanyan Street is named.
Designated a City of San Francisco landmark under Article 10 of the Planning Code as the Stanyan House; one of two single-family dwellings so designated in the Japantown study area.

unknowns: The city's Japantown context statement dates the Stanyan House to between 1852 and 1854; the assessor's roll and Planning's historic resource survey both record 1900.
